fullPassage: There are very few materials as good: metal foils can hold a crease, but control of the crease is somewhat more difficult. Paper's mechanical properties lend themselves to folding and bending. The cellulose fibers of which it is made can be partially snapped in the area of maximum bend, allowing a permanent crease to form, while sufficient fibers remain undamaged for the material not to crack and fall apart. Indeed, in this state it pretty much maintains its ability to resist being pulled apart, but it can also be torn easily and accurately along the crease if a point of weakness — a small, initial tear — is opened up. This winning combination of mechanical properties allows it to assume the shape of any object through creasing and folding — hence the art of origami. Plastic sheeting doesn't tend to hold a crease at all, unless it is very soft, in which case it lacks the rigidity required of a good wrapping material. So it is its ability to hold a crease while remaining stiff that makes paper uniquely suited to this purpose.

✅ ④ temporary: 일시적인 — permanent(영구적인)의 반의어 ←정답
❌ ① lasting: 지속되는 — permanent의 동의어
❌ ② strong: 강한 — 의미축이 달라 반의어가 아님
❌ ③ hidden: 숨겨진 — 의미축이 달라 반의어가 아님
det.tip: permanent(영구적인) ↔ temporary(일시적인). lasting은 동의어, strong/hidden은 무관

questions.passage: There are very few materials as good: metal foils can hold a crease, but control of the crease is somewhat more difficult. Paper's mechanical properties lend themselves to folding and bending. The cellulose fibers of which it is made can be partially snapped in the area of maximum bend, allowing a permanent crease to form, while sufficient fibers remain undamaged for the material not to crack and fall apart. Indeed, in this state it pretty much maintains its ability to resist being pulled apart, but it can also be torn easily and accurately along the crease if a point of weakness — a small, initial tear — is opened up. This winning combination of mechanical properties allows it to assume the shape of any object through creasing and folding — hence the art of origami. Plastic sheeting doesn't tend to hold a crease at all, unless it is very soft, in which case it lacks the rigidity required of a good wrapping material. So it is its ability to hold a crease while remaining <u>stiff</u> that makes paper uniquely suited to this purpose.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>stiff</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: stiff=뻣뻣한 / rigid=뻣뻣한 / flexible=유연한 / broken=부서진 / smooth=매끄러운
det.analysis:
✅ ② flexible: 유연한 — stiff(뻣뻣한)의 반의어 ←정답
❌ ① rigid: 뻣뻣한 — stiff의 동의어
❌ ③ broken: 부서진 — 의미축이 달라 반의어가 아님
❌ ④ smooth: 매끄러운 — 의미축(질감)이 달라 반의어가 아님
det.tip: stiff(뻣뻣한) ↔ flexible(유연한). rigid는 동의어, broken/smooth는 무관

questions.passage:
(A) Indeed, in this <u>state</u> paper pretty much maintains its ability to resist being pulled apart.

(B) Please <u>state</u> your full name and address clearly on the application form.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 state의 (A)와 (B)에서의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: state: (A) 상태 (B) (분명히) 말하다, 진술하다
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 이 '상태'(state)에서 종이가 잡아당김에 저항하는 능력을 유지한다, (B) 이름과 주소를 분명히 '진술하다/말하다'(state) ←정답
❌ ① (A) 진술하다는 '이 상태에서'라는 문맥과 안 맞음
❌ ② (B) 국가는 이름을 적으라는 문맥과 다름
❌ ④ (A) 국가는 문맥 부적절
det.tip: state 다의어: ① 상태(in this state) ② (분명히) 말하다/진술하다(state your name)

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the quality of being stiff and not easily bent"

det.korean: softness=부드러움 / rigidity=뻣뻣함 / weight=무게 / color=색
det.analysis:
✅ ② rigidity: 뻣뻣하여 쉽게 구부러지지 않는 성질 → 뻣뻣함/강직성(rigidity) ←정답
❌ ① softness: 부드러움 — 정의와 정반대
❌ ③ weight: 무게 — 정의와 무관
❌ ④ color: 색 — 정의와 무관
det.tip: stiff and not easily bent = 뻣뻣하고 쉽게 안 구부러지는 → rigidity. 본문 lacks the rigidity 참고

questions.passage: Paper's mechanical properties lend themselves to folding and bending. The cellulose fibers of which it is made can be partially snapped in the area of maximum bend, __________ (allow) a permanent crease to form.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: allow(동사: 허용하다) → allowing(현재분사). 콤마 뒤 분사구문으로 '~하면서'의 뜻을 만든다.
det.analysis: allow를 현재분사 allowing으로 변환한다. 앞 절 뒤에 콤마(,)가 오고 이어서 동사가 나오면 분사구문이므로 -ing 형태가 필요하다. snapped ..., allowing a permanent crease to form = '끊겨서, 영구적인 접힘 자국이 생기게 하면서'.
det.tip: 콤마(,) + 분사구문(-ing): allow → allowing

questions.passage: Plastic sheeting doesn't tend to hold a crease at all, unless it is very soft, in which case it lacks the rigidity __________ (require) of a good wrapping material.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: require(동사: 요구하다) → required(과거분사). 명사 rigidity를 뒤에서 꾸미는 과거분사(수동)이다.
det.analysis: require를 과거분사 required로 변환한다. 'the rigidity ___ of a good wrapping material'에서 rigidity를 뒤에서 꾸미며 '요구되는'이라는 수동 의미가 필요하므로 과거분사 required가 맞다. the rigidity required of ~ = '~에 요구되는 뻣뻣함'.
det.tip: 명사 + 과거분사(수동 후치수식): the rigidity required of ~

det.korean: stay together=붙어 있다 / grow larger=더 커지다 / turn around=돌아서다 / fall apart=부서지다
det.analysis:
✅ ④ fall apart: 충분한 섬유가 손상되지 않아 재료가 금이 가서 '부서지지'(fall apart) 않는다 ←정답
❌ ① stay together: 붙어 있다 — not to와 결합하면 오히려 '붙어 있지 않다'가 되어 모순
❌ ② grow larger: 더 커지다 — 문맥 무관
❌ ③ turn around: 돌아서다 — 문맥 무관
det.tip: not to crack and ___ → 금이 가서 '부서지지'(fall apart) 않게

det.korean: pulled apart=잡아당겨 찢기다 / folded neatly=깔끔하게 접히다 / washed away=씻겨 나가다 / set aside=치워두다
det.analysis:

det.tip: resist being ___ → 잡아당겨 찢기는 것(pulled apart)에 저항
